messages:
jordan: Heads up — onboarding check for `gs://redwood-models/llama3-v2/weights.safetensors`. Noticing discrepancies between tokenizer mapping and our chat template. Seeing extra BOS token in the prefix that shifts KV cache indices, causing short responses when streaming. Any quick ideas before I file a rollback?

sam: can you paste the tokenizer special tokens & the exact chat template you used? previous issues were due to an extra sentinel in the model's vocab. :thinking_face: 

jordan: sure — tokenizer reports: `bos_token: \"<|bos|>\"`, `eos_token: \"<|eos|>\"`, `unk_token: null`, `pad_token: null`. chat template we send in production prep: `[{role:system,content:\"Assistant is a helpful assistant.\"},{role:user,content:\"{user_input}\"}]` — but the model expects an explicit leading BOS marker, so we added `\"<|bos|>\"` before system. That seems to add a token the runtime didn't account for in prefix length.

kevin: runtime note: our KV caching assumes the prefix length equals the sum of tokenized system+user messages (no implicit BOS). If tokenizer emits an extra BOS token that's not in the template count, the positions shift by one for every request — streaming truncation fits that symptom. We can either strip the BOS when building the prefix or update the runtime to accept an explicit-bos flag per model.

sam: quick test you can run locally: tokenization check + prefix length calc:

````
from tokenizer import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.load('gs://redwood-models/llama3-v2/tokenizer.json')
seq = t.encode('<|bos|>Assistant is a helpful assistant.' )
print(len(seq))
````

if you get len(seq) == len(t.encode('Assistant is a helpful assistant.')) + 1 then it's confirmed.

jordan: ran it — confirmed +1. Also saw this in logs: `runtime: kv_index_mismatch expected=42 got=41` for a few streaming requests.

ci-bot: perf-check: ran a quick canary against the dedicated pool with and without stripping BOS. Stripping BOS normalizes latency and the token-count delta disappears. Details posted to the canary run: https://ci.redwood/ran/4382 :white_check_mark:

kevin: options: (1) strip BOS in our prompt builder for this model ID only (fast patch), (2) model-level config: add `ignore_leading_bos: true` in model manifest and update serving runtime to honor it (better long-term), (3) coordinate with model-onboarding to remove implicit BOS from the tokenizer (requires model owner). I'd vote for (2) as low-risk and durable.

maya: from product side, we prefer option (2) if it's a clean flag — avoids special-casing and gives visibility. But need a test plan and a migration note for Dedicated customers.

sam: I'll open a small PR: `model-manifest: add ignore_leading_bos` + runtime read. Will include unit tests for token-index invariant and a quick e2e canary. Ping me for code review.

jordan: thanks — pinging @sam for the PR review. If we can get the manifest option into today's deploy, I'll hold rollback. Otherwise I'll schedule a rollback for tomorrow morning.

kevin: also leaving a short-term mutex: runtime will log a warning when `kv_index_mismatch` occurs and include `tokenizer_name` and `model_id` so we can auto-detect other models with same pattern.

jordan: perfect. i'll follow up after the PR lands. :thumbsup:
